title: samira weights fetch scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Trying to reproduce a customer/private-deploy model load failure on a staging VPC node. Model: open-llama-v2-7b (sharded, 8 shards, safetensors).
- Symptoms: runtime abort during first kv-cache init when loading shard_0001.safetensors. Sometimes fails earlier at shard_0000. Intermittent on different hosts.

Observed errors (snippets):
- RuntimeError: Unexpected EOF while reading file /mnt/models/open-llama/shard_0001.safetensors
- safetensors.DeserializeError: header too large (got 4294967295)
- OSError: mmap failed: [Errno 22] Invalid argument (when mapping >2GB on arm test VM)
- ValueError: mismatched tensor shape for key 'transformer.h.12.attn.q_proj.weight' (expected 4096x4096, got 2048x4096)
- botocore.exceptions.ClientError: An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the GetObject operation: Access Denied (only on one host)

Commands and checks tried (chronological):
1) Basic verifies
   - aws s3 ls s3://redwood-models/open-llama-v2-7b/ --recursive --human-readable
   - aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-models --key open-llama-v2-7b/shard_0001.safetensors -> checked ContentLength/ETag/Metadata
   - aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/open-llama-v2-7b/shard_0001.safetensors /tmp/shard_0001.safetensors && sha256sum /tmp/shard_0001.safetensors
   - Local checksum matched the origin checksum file in the bucket (manifest.json.sha256) on successful downloads.

2) Partial range download test (to rule out range GET / streaming issues):
   - aws s3api get-object --bucket redwood-models --key open-llama-v2-7b/shard_0001.safetensors --range "bytes=0-1048575" partial.bin
   - file partial.bin -> recognized as binary; hexdump of first 64 bytes looked fine (safetensors magic header present)

3) Corruption reproduction attempts
   - Re-uploaded shard_0001 from source storage with: aws s3 cp --acl private --storage-class STANDARD --content-type application/octet-stream shard_0001.safetensors s3://redwood-models/open-llama-v2-7b/
   - Re-downloaded to different host (mac laptop) and attempted to load with safetensors python lib -> success (indicates object in bucket is OK)

4) Host/OS differences
   - Failures concentrated on older staging nodes with kernel 4.x and glibc 2.17. Works on newer ubuntu-22.04 VMs. Hypothesis: mmap of large files or file descriptor limits.
   - On failing hosts, python mmap throws Errno 22 when mapping >2GB. Tried export MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=1 and disabling jemalloc (LD_PRELOAD), no change.

5) Permission/KMS issues
   - One host showed AccessDenied from S3 for same IAM role; that host had different instance profile (forgot to attach CI role). Fixed by reattaching role and re-testing (resolved one class of failures).
   - KMS-encrypted objects: verified with aws s3api head-object {ServerSideEncryption: AWSKMS, SSEKMSKeyId: "arn:aws:kms:..."}. Confirmed node IAM role allowed kms:Decrypt in that account/region.

6) Shard order / manifest mismatch theory
   - Manifest lists shards 0000..0007. Loading logic in runtime enumerates sorted(listdir()) which returned 0000, 0001, 00010 on one host (because of lexical sort) leading to wrong order -> bad tensor shapes at load time.
   - Quick fix: canonicalize with natural sort in loader. Confirmed by running local python snippet to sort numerically and load sequence successfully.

7) Transfer/ETag anomalies
   - Observed ETag mismatch for multi-part uploads (S3 ETag not equal to md5 for multipart). Manifest stored md5 of concatenated parts; mismatch caused checksum compare to fail on some clients. Plan: move to storing sha256 in manifest and use head-object to verify ContentLength + custom sha256 metadata.

8) Runtime efforts
   - Modified loader to try fallback: if safetensors DeserializeError or EOF, attempt to re-download the suspect shard to /tmp with a unique name and re-validate checksum; if still failing, try loading with torch.load (for .pt) if a parallel .pt exists.
   - Added verbose logging to indicate which shard, byte offsets, and object ETag at time of error.

Repro notes (how to trigger locally):
- Emulate lexical sort problem:
  mkdir /tmp/testmodel && touch shard_0000.safetensors shard_0001.safetensors shard_00010.safetensors && python -c "import os;print(sorted(os.listdir('/tmp/testmodel')) )"
  -> shows lexical order; loader that relies on simple sort will get wrong shard order.

- Emulate truncation:
  dd if=/dev/urandom bs=1M count=10 of=shard_0001.safetensors
  Upload truncated object and try loader -> raises Unexpected EOF

Open hypotheses (ranked):
1) Shard name sorting bug in older runtime binary (HIGH): consistent explanation for false tensor shapes. Fix deployed in 2024-10-01 staging binary.
2) mmap + OS limits on older kernels (MED): explains mmap Errno 22 on some hosts. Workaround: fall back to streaming read (no mmap) for >2GB files or use smaller shard sizes.
3) Intermittent partial uploads / multipart ETag mismatch (MED): explains checksum failcases. Need stricter manifest verification and better upload tooling.
4) KMS/role misconfiguration (LOW): human error, resolved for a host but should audit all instance profiles.

Actions taken / next steps (todo):
- [x] Deploy natural sort fix in loader (staging). Confirmed no more bad shapes in canary (2024-10-03).
- [ ] Add streaming-read fallback in runtime for mmap failures (ticket JIRA-INC-3490).
- [ ] Update model publishing pipeline to write sha256 metadata on head-object and store sha256 in manifest (ticket JIRA-MODEL-115).
- [ ] Write small diagnostic script to run on host init that verifies access to S3 + KMS + attempts a small-range GET on each model shard. Add as systemd probe.
- [ ] Audit instance profiles for staging fleet and send doc to infra team (linked_artifacts: JIRA-INC-3421).

Random notes / TODO of quick hacks tried and rolled back:
- Tried piping through gzip to save transfer size; broke safetensors header (obvious in hindsight) -> rolled back.
- Tried copying objects via rclone with resume; worked but hides multipart/etag mismatch, prefer aws cli for clarity.

Contacts/where to look:
- Slack: #infra-model-loading thread "open-llama load flakiness" (search for message id ~16523)
- Ticket: JIRA-INC-3421 (customer report), JIRA-INC-3490 (runtime mmap fallback)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234 (loader natural sort + logging)

If I come back to this later: first re-run failing host with strace on open/read to capture whether read() returns short reads. If kernel-level short reads are happening that's important. Also instrument runtime to write out local shard checksums before mmap so we know the exact bytes on disk.

End of scratchpad.
